messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Weird stan based package problem
parts:
Hey all,

When I build my package in rstudio via the build and reload button, it will build the package fine.

When I use install_github to pull from my git repo, it says bDif.so not available (package name is bDif).

When I manually clone the repo and run R CMD INSTALL on the source, it has the same error. Same with R CMD INSTALL --build.
It only works if I first run R CMD build, then R CMD INSTALL on the resulting tar file.

Is this as intended? It's frustrating that install_github does not work, as it doesn't seem to be building the .so file.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Weird stan based package problem
parts:
On Monday, January 16, 2017 at 7:20:01 PM UTC-5, Stephen Martin wrote:
Hey all,

When I build my package in rstudio via the build and reload button, it will build the package fine.

When I use install_github to pull from my git repo, it says bDif.so not available (package name is bDif).

When I manually clone the repo and run R CMD INSTALL on the source, it has the same error. Same with R CMD INSTALL --build.
It only works if I first run R CMD build, then R CMD INSTALL on the resulting tar file.

Is this as intended? It's frustrating that install_github does not work, as it doesn't seem to be building the .so file.

It sounds like you need to be passing the --preclean argument. See

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm/blob/master/README.md

for how we do it with rstanarm.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Weird stan based package problem
parts:
On Monday, January 16, 2017 at 10:19:00 PM UTC-5, Stephen Martin wrote:
Just for my own edification, why aren't the .cpp files generated in a configure script instead? Isn't configure called by build and install?

The configure{.win} script is called by build but not install (unless you pass --preclean). Also, the Build and Reload button in RStudio passes --preclean, which is not always what you want (it recompiles the C++ even if you have only changed the R), so we came up with an ingenious hack to pass an invalid option called --precleanOOPS that prevents this. Check out the rstanarm.Rproj file on GitHub.

Ben
